summary: Chat session launch lag after serving-runtime heap tuning and model repin
description:
Issue summary:
Customers reported higher-than-usual time-to-first-token (TTFB) when starting chat completions after the 2025-02-11 deployment that included a serving-runtime heap tuning change and a model repin to redwood/gpt-medium-v2-quant. Impact:
- Multiple enterprise customers (notably Acme Finance Inc.) observed median TTFB increase from ~120ms to ~850ms for the first response in chat sessions.
- Some sessions time out on client after 8s, resulting in 504s and session re-tries.
Environment:
- Prod clusters in us-east (primary) and us-west (fallback).
- Deployment on 2025-02-11 contained: runtime heap tuning (gc thresholds lowered), compiler kernel swap, and model pin from -v2 to -v2-quant for cost testing.
Steps to reproduce:
1. Start a new chat session via /v1/chat/completions with model redwood/gpt-medium-v2-quant and streaming=true.
2. Observe initial token emission latency measured by client and server tracing.
3. Repeat across different backend instances and with model pinned to non-quant variant.
Observed behavior:
- First token typically delayed 600ms–1.2s.
- Streaming connection established, but server logs show a pre-generation stall.
- Post-first-token generation latency is normal.
Expected behavior:
- TTFB should remain ~100–200ms for warmed routing and ~200–400ms for cold.
Logs/metrics attached:
- Snapshot traces from request IDs (redacted): r-8f2a, r-9b3c, r-0d1e.
- Dashboard links: latency percentiles, per-model queue depth, GC pause metrics.
Temporary workaround for customer:
- Pin model to redwood/gpt-medium-v2 (non-quant) which restores expected TTFB in ~95% of tests.
- Route high-priority traffic to dedicated capacity pool while we investigate.
Priority justification:
- P1 (Sev1): enterprise customers experiencing degraded UX and some retries/timeouts.
steps_to_reproduce: Create a new chat completion request with model redwood/gpt-medium-v2-quant in prod us-east
Use streaming=true and measure time from request to first token
Repeat with model pin removed and compare latencies
observed_metrics: no sustained increase in per-token generation time after first token
initial_triage: Confirmed spike corresponds to 2025-02-11 deploy window
Heap tuning GC thresholds likely increased pause frequency on cold worker processes
Routing sometimes falls back from deduped warm cache to cold start path for quantized model variant
investigation_notes: Checked deployment changelog: serving-runtime heap tuning and compiler kernel swap merged in PRs linked above
Traces show long pre-generation gap inside worker process between accept() and first token generation, correlates with GC 'stop-the-world' events
Workers running quantized variant exhibit higher memory pressure at session init due to lazy quant init path
Observed that scheduler retry policy increased route churn for model-variant selector under burst, causing more cold handoffs
hypotheses: 1) Heap tuning lowered memory headroom causing GC pauses during session initialization for quantized models
2) Compiler kernel change introduced a lazy initialization path that blocks first-token emission until kernel cache is populated
3) Scheduler affinity changes cause requests to land on cold workers more often post-deploy
tests_run: Reproduced with synthetic loadbench targeting quantized model on us-east: confirmed TTFB increase
Pinned to non-quant model: TTFB normalized
Rolled back compiler kernel swap on a single canary: initial tokens emission improved for canary
temporary_mitigation: Customer routed priority traffic to dedicated pool (confirmed improvement)
Rollback of heap tuning flags on a subset of worker pools for canary
Manual pre-warm of worker processes for quantized models via scheduled warmup requests
resolution: Mitigation in place: rolled back heap tuning on critical us-east pools and disabled lazy kernel init path for quantized models in the canary cluster. These changes reduced median TTFB to ~180ms for canary and brought 95th percentile under 400ms. Permanent fix plan: revert heap tuning globally, apply optimized eager-quant-init for worker startup, and update scheduler affinity algorithm to reduce cold handoffs. Planned changes are tracked in INT-4431 and PRs above.

Implement eager quantization initialization path (owner: serving-runtime)
Add a cache-warm step in deploy pipeline for quantized model variants (owner: scheduler)
Add automated e2e TTFB test to CI gating for runtime-model combined deploys
